html:
The Battle of Mbwila was fought on 29 October 1665 in what is now northern Angola, where a Portuguese army from Luanda defeated the army of the Kingdom of Kongo and killed its king, António I.

The war began over the small state of Mbwila, claimed by both sides, and over Portuguese hopes of mines in Kongo. Portuguese musketeers and African allies, many of them Imbangala, broke the Kongo infantry, and the king's head was taken to Luanda.

After the defeat Kongo fell into decades of civil war between rival claimants, during which São Salvador, the capital, was abandoned. The prophet Kimpa Vita later tried to reunite the kingdom. The battle marked the end of Kongo as a regional power, more than a century after Afonso I.
